aod-9604: Oral Phase 2b obesity RCT: no weight-loss benefit; development discontinued. Early metabolic signals did not translate.
Rodents: lipolysis↑, lipogenesis/weight gain↓; no IGF-1 or long-bone growth effect.
hGH(177–191)-derived analog; no classical GHR binding. Receptor unidentified; hormone-sensitive-lipase involvement unconfirmed.
Oral-trial tolerability resembled placebo. Food-ingredient GRAS status ≠ drug approval. Injectable purity/safety uncertain; WADA-prohibited.
bpc-157: No adequately powered human RCT or Phase 3 support for musculoskeletal/GI claims. Early IBD work used related PL14736.
Broad rodent injury/healing results; single-lineage evidence and publication bias limit confidence.
Proposed NO/NOS, VEGFR2/angiogenesis and GHR effects; direct receptor binding unconfirmed.
Rodent tolerability cannot establish human safety. Long-term, immunogenic and oncologic risks unknown. FDA compounding concerns; WADA-prohibited since 2022.
cagrilintide: REDEFINE-1: n=3,417, 68wk; CagriSema 2.4/2.4mg weight loss 22.7% vs 3.0% placebo; cagrilintide-alone 11.8% vs 2.3%. REDEFINE-2: n=1,206, T2D; 15.7% vs 3.1%. REIMAGINE-2: weight loss 14.2% vs semaglutide 10.2%; HbA1c reduction 1.91% vs 1.76%. CagriSema NDA: 2025-12-18; RENEW monotherapy Phase 3 began Q4-2025.
Aggregation-resistant, albumin-binding amylin analog; ~weekly half-life. Gastric emptying/glucagon↓; satiety↑. GLP-1 combination engages complementary circuits.
Mainly GI events. AE discontinuation: REDEFINE-1 6% vs 3.7%; REDEFINE-2 8.4% vs 3.0%. Two deaths adjudicated unrelated; <⅔ reached maximum dose at 68wk.
cerebrolysin: CARS stroke recovery positive; CASTA primary endpoint negative; CAPTAIN-II TBI signals. Dementia/stroke/TBI evidence heterogeneous, often industry-sponsored; Cochrane conclusions cautious.
Rodent ischemia/TBI/AD: injury, apoptosis and amyloid↓; neurogenesis/neurite growth↑.

Porcine amino-acid/peptide mixture; no isolated active entity. Proposed neurotrophin-like Akt/ERK effects, reduced excitotoxicity/caspase-3 and microglial modulation; single-molecule PK inappropriate.
Injection reactions, dizziness/headache/sweating; hypersensitivity contraindication. Renal/epilepsy precautions; contamination concerns. No FDA approval.
cjc-1295: Teichman 2006: two short RCTs, ages 21–61; GH 2–10× for ≥6d, IGF-1 1.5–3× for 9–11d; repeated-dose elevation ≤28d. Half-life 5.8–8.1d; 30–60mcg/kg best tolerated.
GHRH-knockout mice: growth/GH restored; dose-frequency dependence. Rat albumin conjugation within 15min.
DAC maleimide binds albumin Cys34; D-Ala2 resists DPP-4. GHRHR→cAMP complements GHSR→PLC/IP3; DAC/non-DAC differ.
Injection reactions/flushing/headache. Phase 2 stopped after death judged unrelated coronary disease; full adjudication unavailable. Long-term safety and IGF-1-associated cancer risk unresolved.
dihexa: No controlled human trials or approval; human efficacy/safety unsupported.
Harding-group rat memory and hippocampal-spine findings; independent replication limited.
Stabilized angiotensin-IV peptidomimetic; proposed HGF/c-Met potentiation, not direct c-Met agonism.
Human toxicology/long-term safety unknown; theoretical c-Met-related malignancy risk. Research-product identity/purity uncertain.
dsip: Small older insomnia/pain/withdrawal/depression studies: weak methods, no modern replication or approval.
Rabbit/rat delta-EEG findings inconsistent; pain/seizure/stress effects reported.
Reliable sleep induction and a high-affinity receptor remain unconfirmed; GABA/opioid/HPA mechanisms speculative.
Sparse adverse-event collection; no modern pharmacovigilance. Unregulated-product identity, endotoxin and contamination risks.
epithalon: Small Russian cohorts reported melatonin, retinal and survival signals; limited blinding and independent replication; no modern pivotal RCT.
Originating-group lifespan/tumor/circadian findings; cellular telomerase/telomere effects, little independent replication.
AEDG tetrapeptide; proposed DNA/epigenetic/telomerase actions lack confirmed receptor or independent structural validation.
Reported short-term tolerability does not establish long-term, oncologic or interaction safety; injectable quality uncertain.
follistatin-344: AAV1-FS344 Phase 1/2a Becker-muscular-dystrophy trial improved walking/strength without significant endocrine changes. Gene therapy ≠ injected protein; no controlled protein-injection efficacy evidence.
Transgenic mice: muscle mass +194–327%; mdx AAV effects >2yr; macaque muscle size +15–20%.

FS344→FS315 circulates; FS317→FS288 binds activin/heparan sulfate more strongly. Extracellular myostatin/activin/GDF11 trapping blocks ActRIIB–SMAD2/3; some BMP antagonism. FS288 activin affinity ~10× higher; binding Kd ~50–100pM.
Protein safety unknown: reproductive/FSH effects, BMP-related bone changes, immunogenicity; chorioretinopathy case report. Injected half-life ~90min; WADA-prohibited.
foxo4-dri: No human PK, efficacy or safety trials.
Baar 2017: selective senescent-cell killing; aged-mouse renal, fur and running improvements. Replication/therapeutic-window evidence limited.
Protease-resistant retro-inverso D-peptide displaces p53 from FOXO4, enabling apoptosis; cell-penetrating conjugate delivers intracellularly.
No comprehensive public toxicology package. Off-target p53 activation, immunogenicity, PK and research-product quality remain concerns.
ghk-cu: Small, often sponsored topical studies (n=20–100): skin/wound signals; no large systemic RCT. Historical prezatide approvals do not establish current injectable approval.
Rodent repair/hair and cellular transcription findings; much evidence from Pickart lineage.
GHK shuttles Cu(II), supporting lysyl oxidase, SOD and cytochrome-c oxidase; ECM remodeling better supported than broad transcriptomic claims.
Topical tolerability generally favorable; uncommon dermatitis. Injected safety unknown; copper-overload concern, especially Wilson/copper-handling disorders.
ghrp-2: Human GH responses plus ACTH/cortisol/prolactin rises. Japan approved pralmorelin diagnostic use in October 2004; no FDA therapeutic approval.
Rodent/primate GH/appetite increases; some GH-independent muscle-protection findings.
Potent GHSR agonist; transient HPA/lactotroph activation (~2–3h). Half-life ~15–60min; complements GHRH signaling.
Single-dose diagnostic experience does not establish chronic safety. Appetite/weight gain, cortisol/prolactin and IGF-1 concerns; WADA-prohibited.
ghrp-6: Pandya: nine men, 1mcg/kg IV; GHRH blockade reduced GH AUC 1701→376mcg·min/L (~80%; p<0.001). Other studies confirm hunger/endocrine responses; no pivotal therapeutic trial.
Rodent cardiac, wound and appetite effects; peripheral GH-independent mechanisms proposed.
GHSR→Gq/PLC/IP3/Ca²⁺ releases GH; hypothalamic GHRH/somatostatin and NPY/AgRP regulate pulses/appetite. CD36 contribution proposed.
Acute tolerability does not establish chronic safety: hunger/weight gain, cortisol/prolactin, fluid retention/paresthesias and desensitization. FDA-unapproved; WADA-prohibited.
hexarelin: Strong acute GH release, including older adults; daily dosing produces tachyphylaxis within weeks. Cardiac human studies small; no pivotal efficacy trial.
Independent rodent studies support CD36-associated cardioprotection; largely preclinical.
2-methyl-D-Trp substitution increases potency/persistence versus GHRP-6; cardiac CD36 effects differ from GHSR-mediated GH release.
Short-term tolerability favorable; chronic cardiac safety uncertain. Tachyphylaxis and unregulated-product quality limit extrapolation.
humanin: Human cohorts show age/disease associations only; no published exogenous-humanin intervention trial.
HNG/S14G improves rodent AD, vascular, cardiac and metabolic phenotypes; analog potency differs from native humanin.
MT-RNR2 mitochondrial peptide; BAX/Bim/tBid inhibition and FPR2 or CNTFR/WSX-1/gp130→STAT3 signaling; IGFBP3 binding reported.
Endogenous exposure does not establish pharmacological-dose safety. Human intervention safety and research-product purity/endotoxin control unknown.
igf-1-lr3: No controlled LR3 human trials; mecasermin approval does not extend to LR3. Native-IGF-1 hypoglycemia/GH suppression cannot establish LR3 efficacy/safety.
Muscle/cell assays report ~3× potency; anabolic/satellite-cell findings are preclinical.

83-residue analog: 13-residue extension plus Glu3→Arg; reduced IGFBP binding. IGF1R→PI3K/AKT/mTOR and MAPK; ~20–30h reported half-life; high-concentration hybrid-receptor effects. Reported IR cross-reactivity ~10× lower; hybrid-receptor effects become significant >~500nM.
Hypoglycemia, injection reactions, pain/headache; theoretical proliferation/cancer risk and chorioretinopathy reports. Chronic safety/purity/sterility unestablished; WADA-prohibited.
ipamorelin: Bowel-resection Phase 2: 0.03mg/kg IV twice daily ≤7d; solid-meal tolerance 25.3h vs 32.6h placebo, HR~1.33, p=0.16. No controlled enhancement trials.
GH-release EC50 1.3nM; rat ED50 80nmol/kg. Swine HPA activation remained low at >200× GH-release ED50.
GHSR→Gq/PLC/IP3/Ca²⁺; relatively selective GH release versus other GHRPs; ~2h half-life.
Short trial tolerability cannot establish chronic safety. GH/IGF-1-related edema, paresthesias, insulin resistance and proliferation concerns remain.
kisspeptin: KISS1R genetics establish puberty/GnRH causality. KP54 IVF, amenorrhea/PCOS and HSDD trials show physiological signals; HSDD crossover studies: n=32 women and n=32 men; male tumescence increased ≤56% versus placebo.
Rodent/primate KISS1/KISS1R disruption causes pubertal failure/infertility.
KP54/14/13/10 share amidated RF motif; KP10 minimal. KISS1R→Gq/PLC/Ca²⁺/PKC/ERK. KNDy regulates GnRH pulses; preoptic neurons drive LH surge; KP10 half-life ~4min.
Headache/nausea/injection discomfort; low OHSS signal versus hCG. Chronic safety limited; sustained infusion can desensitize. Analog/formulation results not interchangeable.
kpv: Small topical-dermatology studies suggest benefit; no large RCT or established systemic efficacy. IBD translation remains chiefly preclinical.
Rodent colitis/dermatitis: TNF/IL1β/IL6 and infiltration↓; nanoparticle delivery targets inflamed mucosa.
α-MSH(11–13) tripeptide; proposed intracellular NF-κB modulation, not conventional melanocortin agonism. PepT1/SLC15A1-mediated gut uptake proposed.
Limited short-term tolerability cannot establish systemic/chronic safety. Small size does not prove low clinical immunogenicity; unregulated injection quality remains uncertain.
liraglutide: LEAD/2010: Victoza T2D; SCALE/2014: Saxenda obesity; LEADER: MACE reduction in T2D+CVD. Pediatric T2D ≥10y approved 2019; generics followed in 2024/2025.
Rodent C-cell tumors; human relevance uncertain. Rat fertility unaffected ≤0.6mg/kg.
31-residue GLP-1 analog; Lys26-C16 acylation and Lys34→Arg enable albumin binding, ~13h persistence. GLP1R→cAMP increases glucose-dependent insulin; glucagon/appetite↓.

MTC/MEN2 contraindication; GI, pancreatitis, gallbladder, hypoglycemia, dehydration/renal and allergy risks. Saxenda breast-cancer imbalance (17/2379 vs 3/1300): causality unclear. Antibodies: adults 2.8% (neutralizing 1.2%); pediatric 12% (~1% cross-reactivity).
ll-37: Small topical-wound studies only; no large therapeutic RCT. Endogenous dysregulation contributes to psoriasis/rosacea; deficiency correlates with infection susceptibility.
Rodents: antimicrobial/wound/endotoxin effects; reduced sepsis mortality in some models.
Membrane-disrupting amphipathic helix; context-dependent FPR2 signaling. Self-DNA complexes activate TLR9→IFNα; vitamin-D/VDR induces CAMP.
Small topical studies generally tolerated. Systemic safety unestablished; inflammatory pathophysiology argues against assuming universal benefit.
mazdutide: GLORY-1: n=731, 6mg, 12.55% weight loss; GLORY-2: 9mg, ≤20.1%. DREAMS-3 (n=349): combined HbA1c<7%/weight-loss≥10% endpoint 48% vs semaglutide 21%; HbA1c −2.03% vs −1.84%; weight −10.29% vs −6%. Phase 2 48wk weight losses: 6/10/16mg, 10.5/19.2/22.3% vs placebo 2.2%.
OXM-analog rodent data support insulinotropic/thermogenic effects.
Lipidated weekly GLP1R/GCGR agonist; appetite suppression plus hepatic oxidation/energy expenditure; liver-fat/metabolic improvements reported.
GI effects and dose-related heart-rate increases (<10bpm). Phase 2 treatment-related AEs: 78.1/76.6/82.4% vs placebo 53.2%; worse GI tolerability at 16mg.
melanotan-ii: Small early studies demonstrated pigmentation/erectile effects; no pivotal approval program. MHRA/TGA warn against use; melanoma, altered nevi, priapism and rhabdomyolysis case reports are associations, not proven causation.
Melanocortin animal pharmacology led to bremelanotide development.
Cyclic amidated heptapeptide; MC1/3/4/5R agonist. MC1R drives pigmentation; MC4R mediates central effects; bremelanotide instead has free carboxylate.
Nausea, hypertension, priapism and pigment/oncologic concerns; identity, sterility and endotoxin uncertain. Unapproved medicine.
mots-c: Human circulating-level studies are observational; they do not establish efficacy of exogenous dosing. No published randomized efficacy trial in the reviewed record.
Rodent metabolic/exercise benefits; much evidence from originating group, independent replication incomplete.
Proposed folate/methionine-cycle interference→AICAR→AMPK; stress-related nuclear NRF2 activity. Receptor and exogenous-to-endogenous equivalence unconfirmed.
Human immunogenicity, long-term and off-target safety unknown; rodent tolerability does not establish tissue-specific human AMPK safety.
orforglipron: Foundayo FDA-approved April 1, 2026 for eligible adult weight management; current label and original trial rows retained below. Investigational and marketed tablet doses differ.
Preclinical GLP1R pharmacology supported oral development.
Non-peptide GLP1R agonist; oral only. Label: half-life 29–49h, Vd ~285L after IV research dosing, mainly CYP3A4 metabolism.
GI effects; MTC/MEN2 contraindication; pancreatitis, gallbladder, dehydration/renal and allergy warnings. CYP3A4 interactions; oral-contraceptive backup for 30d after initiation/escalation.
oxytocin: Pitocin: labor induction/augmentation and postpartum hemorrhage. Intranasal trust/social studies do not establish psychiatric efficacy; autism/psychiatric RCT results mixed.
Rodent/primate social recognition, maternal behavior, bonding and HPA findings.
Cyclic nonapeptide; OXTR→Gq, with vasopressin-receptor cross-activity. Myometrial OXTR rises near term; central effects depend on context, including in-group bias.

IV: uterine hyperstimulation/rupture, fetal compromise, water intoxication, cardiovascular effects and coagulopathy-related hemorrhage. Intranasal 20–40IU acute research tolerability ≠ chronic safety. Archived-label cumulative limit: 30units/12h.
pinealon: Small Russian observations, not pivotal controlled evidence; no Phase 3 data.
Cultures/rat models: ROS reduction and cognitive signals; independent replication limited.
Proposed nuclear/DNA interaction of a charged tripeptide; uptake and sequence specificity remain unvalidated.
Adverse-event data insufficient to quantify safety at any dose, duration or population.
pramlintide: FDA 2005: insulin-treated T1D/T2D; 52wk RCTs showed additional HbA1c reduction ~0.3–0.6% and weight-neutral to 1–2kg loss.
Rodent amylin findings support glucagon/gastric-emptying suppression and satiety.
CTR+RAMP1/2/3 agonist; A25P/S28P/S29P reduce aggregation. Complements insulin; does not replace it or activate insulin/GLP1 receptors.
Boxed severe-hypoglycemia risk with insulin, especially ≤3h. Label reduces initial mealtime insulin 50%. Nausea common; gastroparesis/hypoglycemia-unawareness/monitoring limitations preclude use.
pt-141: RECONNECT: two 24wk Phase 3 RCTs supported 2019 approval for acquired, generalized HSDD in premenopausal women; desire/distress benefits modest but significant.
Rodent/primate central sexual effects depend on MC4R.
On-demand SC melanocortin agonist; free-carboxylate melanotan-II analog. MC4R mediates desire; peripheral MC1R drives pigmentation.
Contraindicated: uncontrolled hypertension/CVD. BP ~+6mmHg; HR −2–3bpm, usually resolves ≤12h. Nausea ~40%; pigmentation may persist. Label caps: 1dose/24h, 8doses/month.
retatrutide: Investigational; FDA-unapproved. TRIUMPH-4: n=445, 68wk, obesity/knee-OA; 12mg topline weight loss ~28.7% with pain improvement. Phase 2: ~24% at 48wk; outcome trials ongoing.
Triple-receptor animal pharmacology supports development; less published evidence than approved incretins.
Weekly lipidated GIPR/GLP1R/GCGR agonist; insulin/satiety plus glucagon-driven hepatic metabolism. Exact activity ratio proprietary.
GI effects; dose-dependent dysesthesia (~20.9% at 12mg in secondary reporting). Long-term cancer/CV outcomes unresolved; non-trial supply quality unestablished.
selank: Russian anxiety/neurasthenia studies suggest benzodiazepine-comparable effects; no large independent replication or FDA/EMA registration.
Rodent anxiety/withdrawal and IMR-32 GABA-expression findings; splenic immune-transcription effects.
Tuftsin+PGP resists degradation; proposed GABAergic transcription modulation, not direct benzodiazepine-like GABA-A agonism. Enkephalinase/serotonin/BDNF effects reported.
Short-term Russian reports: little cognitive impairment/dependence/withdrawal; independent chronic-safety and pharmacovigilance data absent.
semaglutide: SUSTAIN/PIONEER: T2D; STEP: obesity; SELECT (>17,600): MACE 6.5% vs 8% placebo. ESSENCE: noncirrhotic MASH F2–F3 accelerated approval in 2025; formulations/indications differ.
Rodent thyroid C-cell tumors; human relevance uncertain.
Aib8 and Lys26-C18 modifications support DPP-4 resistance/albumin binding; ~weekly injectable persistence. GLP1R→cAMP; insulin↑, glucagon/appetite/gastric emptying↓.
MTC/MEN2 contraindication; GI, pancreatic/gallbladder, hypoglycemia, dehydration/renal, allergy, retinopathy and heart-rate warnings; SELECT fracture imbalance in ≥75y. Consult current product label.
semax: Russian stroke/vascular registration and clinical experience; independent pivotal replication and healthy-adult cognitive evidence lacking. No FDA/EMA approval.
Rat ischemia: BDNF/NGF/TrkB and phospho-CREB↑; inflammatory genes/MMP9/c-Fos/JNK↓.
ACTH(4–7)+PGP resists degradation; no classical MC2R steroidogenic action. Brain melanocortin/transcriptional and TrkB/Akt effects reported.
Local acute events generally mild; chronic non-Russian safety and sustained neurotrophin/autonomic effects uncertain.
sermorelin: Geref pediatric approval 1997; discontinued 2008, not for safety/efficacy. Diagnostic GH-reserve use established; adult anti-aging/body-composition RCT evidence limited. Compounded products do not inherit Geref approval.
Rodent/primate GHRHR→pulsatile GH/IGF-1 with feedback preserved.
GHRH(1–29); short ~10–15min plasma half-life. Somatostatin/IGF-1 feedback remains; no GHSR appetite/HPA action.
Mainly injection reactions. Chronic IGF-1 elevation raises theoretical malignancy concerns; preserved feedback does not prove chronic enhancement safety.
snap-8: Mostly manufacturer-sponsored topical wrinkle studies; independent controlled evidence and effective neuromuscular penetration unestablished.
In-vitro SNARE inhibition; limited intact-skin/animal translation.
SNAP25-mimetic octapeptide proposed to inhibit SNARE assembly/acetylcholine release. Poor skin penetration leaves hydration/excipient explanations possible.
Topical irritation possible; low absorption limits systemic exposure. Injectable use unrecognized and safety unknown.
ss-31: Forzinity: accelerated FDA approval for Barth syndrome, ≥30kg. MMPOWER-3 and randomized TAZPOWER primary endpoints were negative; extension signals supported development. Confirmatory benefit required; ophthalmic studies mixed.
Independently replicated mitochondrial/cardiac/renal/neural benefits in animals.

Cardiolipin-binding aromatic-cationic tetrapeptide; stabilizes cristae/cytochrome-c/ETC organization. ROS↓ and ATP efficiency↑; not stoichiometric ROS scavenging. Reported inner-membrane enrichment: 1000–5000×.
Injection reactions common (>30% in some studies); headache/nausea/dizziness and hypersensitivity possible. Long-term healthy-adult safety unestablished.
survodutide: Phase 2 obesity: n~387, 46wk completers, ~18.7–19% weight loss. MASH resolution without fibrosis worsening: ≤62% vs ~14% placebo. T2D 16wk HbA1c response; Phase 3 obesity/MASH/CV programs ongoing.
GLP1R-biased GLP1R/GCGR agonist combines glycemic/appetite effects with hepatic oxidation; avoids excessive glucagon-driven hyperglycemia at studied doses.
Mainly GI events; definitive Phase 3 outcome safety pending.
tb-500: Mixed local Tβ4 eye/wound trials; no FDA approval or large systemic musculoskeletal/athletic-recovery RCT.
Broad preclinical cardiac/corneal/skin/neural repair and fibrosis evidence; independently replicated mechanisms.
LKKTETQ binds G-actin 1:1; supports migration/angiogenesis. Ac-SDKP cleavage may mediate antifibrosis; marketed TB-500 identity varies.
Local trial tolerability cannot establish systemic safety. Theoretical occult-cancer/angiogenesis risk; purity/endotoxin/identity concerns. WADA-prohibited.
tb4-frag: RGN-259 eye and RGN-137 skin trials mixed; small IV cardiac/stroke and Ac-SDKP studies exploratory. No approved product.
Rodent/porcine cardiac, corneal/dermal, neural and antifibrotic findings.
Intact Tβ4 sequesters actin 1:1; Ac-SDKP has distinct antifibrotic biology. No single validated cell-surface receptor; fragments cannot inherit parent evidence.
Early local/IV tolerability data limited; systemic/chronic pharmacovigilance insufficient. Research-product purity/endotoxin/identity unknown; WADA-prohibited.
teduglutide: STEPS programs: ≥20% parenteral-support reduction at 24wk favored treatment; extensions showed durability. FDA adult approval 2012; pediatric ≥1y approval 2019.
Rodent GLP2R trophic studies support villus/crypt growth.
A2G resists DPP-4. GLP2R→Gs acts through enteric/stromal paracrine IGF1/EGF signaling; distinct from GLP1 incretins.

Neoplasia/polyps require endoscopic surveillance; obstruction, biliary/pancreatic disease and fluid overload risks. Abdominal/injection reactions common; benefit-risk applies to parenteral-dependent SBS.
tesamorelin: Two 26wk Phase 3 HIV-lipohypertrophy RCTs: 2mg SC/day reduced VAT; IGF-1 steady state ~2wk. Weight neutral, not general weight-loss therapy.
Rat offspring hydrocephaly at ~2–4× human exposure during organogenesis/lactation.
44-residue modified GHRH; GHRHR→cAMP/PKA→GH→hepatic JAK2/STAT5/IGF1 and adipose lipolysis; feedback largely preserved.

Edema, arthralgia/injection reactions, carpal-tunnel symptoms and glucose intolerance. Contraindications: malignancy, disrupted pituitary axis, pregnancy, hypersensitivity; long-term CV safety unestablished.
thymosin-alpha-1: Regional hepatitis/oncology adjunct use; no FDA approval. US HCV Phase 3 endpoint missed. COVID associations observational; sepsis evidence suggestive, not definitive.
Rodent infection/tumor/immunosuppression studies support dendritic/T/NK recovery and vaccine responses.
PTMA-derived 28-mer; proposed TLR9→MyD88/IRAK→IRF7/IFN or NF-κB; Th1/CD8/NK modulation. TLR2/4 and exhausted-T-cell restoration less established.
Mostly injection reactions in labeled-use experience; autoimmune exacerbation plausible. Favorable regional experience does not establish safety for every immune condition.
thymulin: Small, dated immunodeficiency/arthritis/pediatric-infection pilots; no modern RCT or approval. Circulating activity used as zinc/thymus biomarker.
Rodents: zinc-dependent anti-inflammatory, antipyretic and thymic-restoration signals.
Zinc-dependent pyroglutamyl nonapeptide; chelation abolishes activity. Specific receptor unidentified; T-cell/cytokine mechanisms inferred.
Human pharmacological-dose safety unstudied. Endogenous picomolar exposure cannot establish exogenous safety; zinc saturation/purity uncertain.
tirzepatide: SURPASS: T2D; SURMOUNT: obesity/OSA. OSA AHI reductions: PAP users ~29 vs ~6events/h placebo; nonusers ~25 vs ~5. Weight loss ~45–50 vs ~4–6lb.
Rodent C-cell tumors underlie boxed warning.
Modified 39-mer GIP backbone, Aib2/13 and Lys20-C20 acylation; ~5d half-life. GIPR/GLP1R→cAMP; insulin↑, appetite/glucagon/gastric emptying↓; OSA improvement accompanies weight loss.
MTC/MEN2 and serious-allergy contraindications; GI, pancreatic/gallbladder, hypoglycemia, dehydration/renal and retinopathy risks. Product-specific current labeling governs use.
vip: Regional Invicorp (aviptadil+phentolamine) ED evidence; COVID-ARDS Phase 3 failed its primary endpoint. Pulmonary/sarcoidosis studies mixed; no FDA indication.
Vasodilatory/bronchodilatory/immune effects in sepsis, autoimmunity, asthma and ischemia models.
VPAC1/2→Gs/cAMP/PKA; tissue-dependent Gq cross-talk, NF-κB suppression/IL10 modulation and smooth-muscle relaxation; shares PACAP pathways.
Flushing, hypotension/tachycardia; intracavernosal priapism/bruising/fibrosis risks. Systemic/ICU exposure requires blood-pressure monitoring.
hcg: Product-specific ovulation/ART, male hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and pediatric cryptorchidism indications; testosterone/spermatogenesis may improve. Descent often incomplete, requiring surgery. Urinary and recombinant products differ.
Glycosylated hCG→LHCGR→Gs/cAMP/PKA→StAR/CYP11A1/CYP17A1/HSD3B2→gonadal steroids; ERK effects. β-subunit glycosylation prolongs exposure versus LH.
OHSS, thrombosis/multiple gestation, anaphylaxis; estradiol/gynecomastia and precocious puberty risks. No weight-loss approval.
mk-677: Nass: n=65, age60–81, 25mg/day for12mo; fat-free mass +~1.6kg, no strength/function benefit. Alzheimer RCT n=563: IGF-1 +60–73%, no cognitive benefit. Hip-fracture RCT n=123 stopped for CHF imbalance.
Rat/dog GH/IGF-1 and appetite effects; ACTH/cortisol responses reported.
Non-peptide GHSR→Gq/PLC/IP3/Ca²⁺/PKC→GH→hepatic JAK2/STAT5/IGF1; NPY/AgRP drives hunger.
CHF 4/62 vs 1/61 in frail elderly (~80y); younger-population risk unknown. Edema, hyperglycemia/insulin resistance, appetite/cortisol increases. FDA-unapproved; WADA-prohibited.
5-amino-1mq: No published completed human Phase 1/2 efficacy/safety evidence in reviewed sources; community use is anecdotal.
Mice: 20mg/kg/day reversed diet-induced obesity without lower food intake. Aged-female 10mg/kg/day, 8wk: grip +~25% alone, ~60% with exercise; cancer-model work exploratory.
NNMT inhibition preserves nicotinamide/NAMPT salvage, NAD⁺ and SAM; MNA/lipogenesis↓. Human PK cannot be inferred from rat results.
Rodent 5–20mg/kg tolerability does not establish human chronic, reproductive or genotoxic safety. Human distribution/elimination and vendor purity uncertain.
